  description: 'Mechanism profile for seed ''phonet: pep: fix use-after-free in pep_get_sb()''. UNTRUSTED SOURCE: network-received packet payloads parsed in protocol RX handlers; here a Phonet pipe control skb whose first bytes (sb_len, sb_type) are fully attacker-controlled, including the length field that drives how far the skb must be linearized. MISSING GUARANTEE: lifetime/representation invariant that a raw pointer into skb->head/skb->data is invalidated whenever a linearization or head-reallocation helper (pskb_may_pull, __pskb_pull_tail, skb_linearize, pskb_expand_head, skb_cow*, skb_unclone) may relocate the head buffer; code assumed skb_header_pointer() results stay valid across such calls. No revalidation/refetch, no copy-out of the header before the pull. UNSAFE USE: after pskb_may_pull(skb, ph->sb_len) potentially reallocates the head, the stale pre-pull pointer ph is dereferenced for both read (ph->sb_type) and write (ph->sb_len -= 2) — a state transition through freed slab memory. CONSEQUENCE: slab use-after-free read/write on the RX path reachable from an unauthenticated/untrusted peer packet; KASAN-detectable UAF, potential info leak or memory corruption. TRANSFERABLE INVARIANT: any code that captures a pointer into a buffer that a subsequent call may realloc/free (skb head linearization being the canonical case) and dereferences it afterward without refetching is the same bug class, independent of protocol. BRANCHES: rx-pull-stale-hdr=receive-path protocol parsers (net/* *_rcv/_recv/_do_rcv handlers) that cache a header pointer via skb_header_pointer or a direct skb->data cast before calling pskb_may_pull/pskb_pull/__pskb_pull_tail and then read or write through the stale pointer after the pull; tx-cow-head-realloc=transmit/edit paths (tunnel xmit, neighbor, netfilter mangle, encapsulation) where a pointer into skb headers survives a call documented to reallocate the head (skb_cow_head, skb_cow, skb_unclone, skb_share_check, pskb_expand_head, skb_linearize) and is reused without refetch; loop-parser-stale-state=variable-length record/TLV parse loops and ''get next record'' helpers where a pull/linearize happens inside the loop body or helper while pointer, offset, or length state captured in an earlier iteration remains live and is dereferenced in a later one (the seed''s pep_get_sb is exactly such a helper); gro-frag-stale-ptr=GRO/segmentation/frag-list paths where pointers into per-packet headers (skb_gro_header_pointer, skb_gro_header_slow results, pointers into frag-list data) are held across skb_gro_pull/pskb_may_pull over frag lists and become stale after head relocation or frag consumption.'

Author: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
Date:   Tue Jul 21 01:58:45 2026 -0700

    phonet: pep: fix use-after-free in pep_get_sb()
    
    pep_get_sb() doesn't consider that pskb_may_pull() might have relocated
    the skb data, and continue to access the older pointer, causing UAF.
    
    Reproduced under KASAN:
    
      BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in pep_get_sb+0x234/0x3b0

       pipe_handler_do_rcv+0x5f7/0xa10
       pep_do_rcv+0x203/0x410
       __sk_receive_skb+0x471/0x4a0
       phonet_rcv+0x5b3/0x6c0
       __netif_receive_skb+0xcc/0x1d0
    
    Refetch the header with skb_header_pointer() after pskb_may_pull(), so
    the possibly stale pointer is no longer dereferenced. There are better
    ways to solve this, but, this is the less instrusive one.
    
    Fixes: 9641458d3ec4 ("Phonet: Pipe End Point for Phonet Pipes protocol")
    Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
    Signed-off-by: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
    Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260721-phonet_get_sb_uaf-v1-1-95fd7881cc4e@debian.org
    Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/phonet/pep.c b/net/phonet/pep.c
index 706927139393..31b29e3ca7bc 100644
--- a/net/phonet/pep.c
+++ b/net/phonet/pep.c
@@ -55,6 +55,8 @@ static unsigned char *pep_get_sb(struct sk_buff *skb, u8 *ptype, u8 *plen,
 	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	if (ph == NULL || ph->sb_len < 2 || !pskb_may_pull(skb, ph->sb_len))
 		return NULL;
+	/* pskb_may_pull() may have reallocated the head; refetch ph. */
+	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	ph->sb_len -= 2;
 	*ptype = ph->sb_type;
 	*plen = ph->sb_len;
"
}
